transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And thank you for agreeing to moderate this debate this evening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you to Lynn University for welcoming us here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, it’s good to be with you again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We were together at a humorous event a little earlier, and it’s nice to maybe funny this time, not on purpose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ll see what happens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is obviously an area of great concern to the entire world, and to America in particular, which is to see a — a complete change in the — the structure and the — the environment in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: With the Arab Spring, came a great deal of hope that there would be a change towards more moderation, and opportunity for greater participation on the part of women in public life, and in economic life in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But instead, we’ve seen in nation after nation, a number of disturbing events.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Of course we see in Syria, 30,000 civilians having been killed by the military there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We see in — in Libya, an attack apparently by, I think we know now, by terrorists of some kind against — against our people there, four people dead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our hearts and — and minds go out to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mali has been taken over, the northern part of Mali by al-Qaeda type individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have in — in Egypt, a Muslim Brotherhood president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so what we’re seeing is a pretty dramatic reversal in the kind of hopes we had for that region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Of course the greatest threat of all is Iran, four years closer to a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and we’re going to have to recognize that we have to do as the president has done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I congratulate him on — on taking out Osama bin Laden and going after the leadership in al-Qaeda.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But we can’t kill our way out of this mess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to put in place a very comprehensive and robust strategy to help the — the world of Islam and other parts of the world, reject this radical violent extremism, which is — it’s certainly not on the run.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s certainly not hiding.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a group that is now involved in 10 or 12 countries, and it presents an enormous threat to our friends, to the world, to America, long term, and we must have a comprehensive strategy to help reject this kind of extremism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, my first job as commander in chief, Bob, is to keep the American people safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what we’ve done over the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We ended the war in Iraq, refocused our attention on those who actually killed us on 9/11.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence, Al Qaeda’s core leadership has been decimated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In addition, we’re now able to transition out of Afghanistan in a responsible way, making sure that Afghans take responsibility for their own security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that allows us also to rebuild alliances and make friends around the world to combat future threats.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now with respect to Libya, as I indicated in the last debate, when we received that phone call, I immediately made sure that, number one, that we did everything we could to secure those Americans who were still in harm’s way; number two, that we would investigate exactly what happened, and number three, most importantly, that we would go after those who killed Americans and we would bring them to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s exactly what we’re going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think it’s important to step back and think about what happened in Libya.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Keep in mind that I and Americans took leadership in organizing an international coalition that made sure that we were able to, without putting troops on the ground at the cost of less than what we spent in two weeks in Iraq, liberate a country that had been under the yoke of dictatorship for 40 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Got rid of a despot who had killed Americans and as a consequence, despite this tragedy, you had tens of thousands of Libyans after the events in Benghazi marching and saying America is our friend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We stand with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now that represents the opportunity we have to take advantage of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, Governor Romney, I’m glad that you agree that we have been successful in going after Al Qaida, but I have to tell you that, you know, your strategy previously has been one that has been all over the map and is not designed to keep Americans safe or to build on the opportunities that exist in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, my strategy is pretty straightforward, which is to go after the bad guys, to make sure we do our very best to interrupt them, to — to kill them, to take them out of the picture.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But my strategy is broader than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s — that’s important, of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the key that we’re going to have to pursue is a — is a pathway to get the Muslim world to be able to reject extremism on its own.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t want another Iraq, we don’t want another Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the right course for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The right course for us is to make sure that we go after the — the people who are leaders of these various anti-American groups and these — these jihadists, but also help the Muslim world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And how do we do that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A group of Arab scholars came together, organized by the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: , to look at how we can help the — the world reject these — these terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the answer they came up with was this: One, more economic development.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We should key our foreign aid, our direct foreign investment, and that of our friends, we should coordinate it to make sure that we — we push back and give them more economic development.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, better education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number three, gender equality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number four, the rule of law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to help these nations create civil societies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But what’s been happening over the last couple of years is, as we’ve watched this tumult in the Middle East, this rising tide of chaos occur, you see Al Qaida rushing in, you see other jihadist groups rushing in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and they’re throughout many nations in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s wonderful that Libya seems to be making some progress, despite this terrible tragedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But next door, of course, we have Egypt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Libya’s 6 million population; Egypt, 80 million population.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We want — we want to make sure that we’re seeing progress throughout the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: With Mali now having North Mali taken over by Al Qaida; with Syria having Assad continuing to — to kill, to murder his own people, this is a region in tumult.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, of course, Iran on the path to a nuclear weapon, we’ve got real .

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney, I’m glad that you recognize that Al Qaida is a threat, because a few months ago when you were asked what’s the biggest geopolitical threat facing America, you said Russia, not Al Qaida; you said Russia, in the 1980s, they’re now calling to ask for their foreign policy back because, you know, the Cold War’s been over for 20 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But Governor, when it comes to our foreign policy, you seem to want to import the foreign policies of the 1980s, just like the social policies of the 1950s and the economic policies of the 1920s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You say that you’re not interested in duplicating what happened in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But just a few weeks ago, you said you think we should have more troops in Iraq right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the — the challenge we have — I know you haven’t been in a position to actually execute foreign policy — but every time you’ve offered an opinion, you’ve been wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You said we should have gone into Iraq, despite that fact that there were no weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You said that we should still have troops in Iraq to this day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You indicated that we shouldn’t be passing nuclear treaties with Russia despite the fact that 71 senators, Democrats and Republicans, voted for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You said that, first, we should not have a timeline in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Then you said we should.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now you say maybe or it depends, which means not only were you wrong, but you were also confusing in sending mixed messages both to our troops and our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, what — what we need to do with respect to the Middle East is strong, steady leadership, not wrong and reckless leadership that is all over the map.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And unfortunately, that’s the kind of opinions that you’ve offered throughout this campaign, and it is not a recipe for American strength, or keeping America safe over the long haul.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, of course I don’t concur with what the president said about my own record and the things that I’ve said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They don’t happen to be accurate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But — but I can say this, that we’re talking about the Middle East and how to help the Middle East reject the kind of terrorism we’re seeing, and the rising tide of tumult and — and confusion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and attacking me is not an agenda.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Attacking me is not talking about how we’re going to deal with the challenges that exist in the Middle East, and take advantage of the opportunity there, and stem the tide of this violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I’ll respond to a couple of things that you mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First of all, Russia I indicated is a geopolitical foe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Not…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s a geopolitical foe, and I said in the same — in the same paragraph I said, and Iran is the greatest national security threat we face.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Russia does continue to battle us in the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: time and time again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I have clear eyes on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to wear rose-colored glasses when it comes to Russia, or Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Putin.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I’m certainly not going to say to him, I’ll give you more flexibility after the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: After the election, he’ll get more backbone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, with regards to Iraq, you and I agreed I believe that there should be a status of forces agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Oh you didn’t?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You didn’t want a status of…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I would not have had done was left 10,000 troops in Iraq that would tie us down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that certainly would not help us in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry, you actually — there was a — there was an effort on the part of the president to have a status of forces agreement, and I concurred in that, and said that we should have some number of troops that stayed on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That was something I concurred with…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …that your posture.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That was my posture as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You thought it should have been 5,000 troops…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … I thought there should have been more troops, but you know what?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The answer was we got…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … no troops through whatsoever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This was just a few weeks ago that you indicated that we should still have troops in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, I…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …I’m sorry that’s a…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You — you…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …that’s a — I indicated…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …major speech.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …I indicated that you failed to put in place a status…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …of forces agreement at the end of the conflict that existed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor — here — here’s — here’s one thing…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …here’s one thing I’ve learned as commander in chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to be clear, both to our allies and our enemies, about where you stand and what you mean.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You just gave a speech a few weeks ago in which you said we should still have troops in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is not a recipe for making sure that we are taking advantage of the opportunities and meeting the challenges of the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it is absolutely true that we cannot just meet these challenges militarily.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so what I’ve done throughout my presidency and will continue to do is, number one, make sure that these countries are supporting our counterterrorism efforts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, make sure that they are standing by our interests in Israel’s security, because it is a true friend and our greatest ally in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number three, we do have to make sure that we’re protecting religious minorities and women because these countries can’t develop unless all the population, not just half of it, is developing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number four, we do have to develop their economic — their economic capabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But number five, the other thing that we have to do is recognize that we can’t continue to do nation building in these regions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Part of American leadership is making sure that we’re doing nation building here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That will help us maintain the kind of American leadership that we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we’ve done is organize the international community, saying Assad has to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve mobilized sanctions against that government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have made sure that they are isolated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have provided humanitarian assistance and we are helping the opposition organize, and we’re particularly interested in making sure that we’re mobilizing the moderate forces inside of Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But ultimately, Syrians are going to have to determine their own future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so everything we’re doing, we’re doing in consultation with our partners in the region, including Israel which obviously has a huge interest in seeing what happens in Syria; coordinating with Turkey and other countries in the region that have a great interest in this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This — what we’re seeing taking place in Syria is heartbreaking, and that’s why we are going to do everything we can to make sure that we are helping the opposition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to recognize that, you know, for us to get more entangled militarily in Syria is a serious step, and we have to do so making absolutely certain that we know who we are helping; that we’re not putting arms in the hands of folks who eventually could turn them against us or allies in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I am confident that Assad’s days are numbered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what we can’t do is to simply suggest that, as Governor Romney at times has suggested, that giving heavy weapons, for example, to the Syrian opposition is a simple proposition that would lead us to be safer over the long term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: SCHIEFFER: Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, let’s step back and talk about what’s happening in Syria and how important it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First of all, 30,000 people being killed by their government is a humanitarian disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, Syria is an opportunity for us because Syria plays an important role in the Middle East, particularly right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Syria is Iran’s only ally in the Arab world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s their route to the sea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s the route for them to arm Hezbollah in Lebanon, which threatens, of course, our ally, Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so seeing Syria remove Assad is a very high priority for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, seeing a — a replacement government being responsible people is critical for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And finally, we don’t want to have military involvement there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t want to get drawn into a military conflict.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so the right course for us, is working through our partners and with our own resources, to identify responsible parties within Syria, organize them, bring them together in a — in a form of — if not government, a form of — of — of council that can take the lead in Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then make sure they have the arms necessary to defend themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We do need to make sure that they don’t have arms that get into the — the wrong hands.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Those arms could be used to hurt us down the road.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to make sure as well that we coordinate this effort with our allies, and particularly with — with Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the Saudi’s and the Qatari, and — and the Turks are all very concerned about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re willing to work with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to have a very effective leadership effort in Syria, making sure that the — the insurgent there are armed and that the insurgents that become armed, are people who will be the responsible parties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Recognize — I believe that Assad must go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I believe he will go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I believe — we want to make sure that we have the relationships of friendship with the people that take his place, steps that in the years to come we see Syria as a — as a friend, and Syria as a responsible party in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This — this is a critical opportunity for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what I’m afraid of is we’ve watched over the past year or so, first the president saying, well we’ll let the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: deal with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And Assad — excuse me, Kofi Annan came in and said we’re going to try to have a ceasefire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That didn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Then it went to the Russians and said, let’s see if you can do something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We should be playing the leadership role there, not on the ground with military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …by the leadership role.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are playing the leadership role.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We organized the Friends of Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are mobilizing humanitarian support, and support for the opposition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are making sure that those we help are those who will be friends of ours in the long term and friends of our allies in the region over the long term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But going back to Libya — because this is an example of how we make choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When we went in to Libya, and we were able to immediately stop the massacre there, because of the unique circumstances and the coalition that we had helped to organize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We also had to make sure that Moammar Gadhafi didn’t stay there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And to the governor’s credit, you supported us going into Libya and the coalition that we organized.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when it came time to making sure that Gadhafi did not stay in power, that he was captured, Governor, your suggestion was that this was mission creep, that this was mission muddle.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Imagine if we had pulled out at that point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, Moammar Gadhafi had more American blood on his hands than any individual other than Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so we were going to make sure that we finished the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of the reason why the Libyans stand with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we did so in a careful, thoughtful way, making certain that we knew who we were dealing with, that those forces of moderation on the ground were ones that we could work with, and we have to take the same kind of steady, thoughtful leadership when it comes to Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly what we’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to have our military involved in Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think there is a necessity to put our military in Syria at this stage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t anticipate that in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As I indicated, our objectives are to replace Assad and to have in place a new government which is friendly to us, a responsible government, if possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I want to make sure they get armed and they have the arms necessary to defend themselves, but also to remove — to remove Assad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I do not want to see a military involvement on the part of our — of our troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And this isn’t — this isn’t going to be necessary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We — we have, with our partners in the region, we have sufficient resources to support those groups.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But look, this has been going on for a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a time — this should have been a time for American leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We should have taken a leading role, not militarily, but a leading role organizationally, governmentally to bring together the parties; to find responsible parties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As you hear from intelligence sources even today, the — the insurgents are highly disparate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They haven’t come together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They haven’t formed a unity group, a council of some kind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That needs to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: America can help that happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And we need to make sure they have the arms they need to carry out the very important role which is getting rid of Assad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ll — I’ll be very quick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What you just heard Governor Romney said is he doesn’t have different ideas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s because we’re doing exactly what we should be doing to try to promote a moderate Syrian leadership and a — an effective transition so that we get Assad out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of leadership we’ve shown.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of leadership we’ll continue to show.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t, because I think that America has to stand with democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The notion that we would have tanks run over those young people who were in Tahrir Square, that is not the kind of American leadership that John F.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Kennedy talked about 50 years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what I’ve also said is that now that you have a democratically elected government in Egypt, that they have to make sure that they take responsibility for protecting religious minorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we have put significant pressure on them to make sure they’re doing that; to recognize the rights of women, which is critical throughout the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These countries can’t develop if young women are not given the kind of education that they need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They have to abide by their treaty with Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is a red line for us, because not only is Israel’s security at stake, but our security is at stake if that unravels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They have to make sure that they’re cooperating with us when it comes to counterterrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we will help them with respect to developing their own economy, because ultimately what’s going to make the Egyptian revolution successful for the people of Egypt, but also for the world, is if those young people who gathered there are seeing opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Their aspirations are similar to young people’s here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They want jobs, they want to be able to make sure their kids are going to a good school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They want to make sure that they have a roof over their heads and that they have the prospects of a better life in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so one of the things that we’ve been doing is, is, for example, organizing entrepreneurship conferences with these Egyptians to give them a sense of how they can start rebuilding their economy in a way that’s noncorrupt, that’s transparent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what is also important for us to understand is, is that for America to be successful in this region there’s some things that we’re going to have to do here at home as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, one of the challenges over the last decade is we’ve done experiments in nation building in places like Iraq and Afghanistan and we’ve neglected, for example, developing our own economy, our own energy sectors, our own education system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s very hard for us to project leadership around the world when we’re not doing what we need to do…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I believe, as the president indicated, and said at the time that I supported his — his action there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I felt that — I wish we’d have had a better vision of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I wish that, looking back at the beginning of the president’s term and even further back than that, that we’d have recognized that there was a growing energy and passion for freedom in that part of the world, and that we would have worked more aggressively with our friend and with other friends in the region to have them make the transition towards a more representative form of government, such that it didn’t explode in the way that it did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But once it exploded, I felt the same as the president did, which is these freedom voices and the streets of Egypt, where the people who were speaking of our principles and the President Mubarak had done things which were unimaginable and the idea of him crushing his people was not something that we could possibly support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me step back and talk about what I think our mission has to be in the Middle East and even more broadly, because our purpose is to make sure the world is more — is peaceful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We want a peaceful planet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We want people to be able to enjoy their lives and know they’re going to have a bright and prosperous future, not be at war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s our purpose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the mantle of leadership for the — promoting the principles of peace has fallen to America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t ask for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But it’s an honor that we have it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But for us to be able to promote those principles of peace requires us to be strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that begins with a strong economy here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, the economy is not stronger.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When the — when the president of Iraq — excuse me, of Iran, Ahmadinejad, says that our debt makes us not a great country, that’s a frightening thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Former chief of the — Joint Chiefs of Staff said that — Admiral Mullen said that our debt is the biggest national security threat we face.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This — we have weakened our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need a strong economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to have as well a strong military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our military is second to none in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re blessed with terrific soldiers, and extraordinary technology and intelligence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the idea of a trillion dollar in cuts through sequestration and budget cuts to the military would change that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to have strong allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our association and connection with our allies is essential to America’s strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re the great nation that has allies, 42 allies and friends around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, finally, we have to stand by our principles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if we’re strong in each of those things, American influence will grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But unfortunately, in nowhere in the world is America’s influence will grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But unfortunately, in — nowhere in the world is America’s influence greater today than it was four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that’s because we’ve become weaker in each of those four…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well I — I absolutely believe that America has a — a responsibility, and the privilege of helping defend freedom and promote the principles that — that make the world more peaceful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And those principles include human rights, human dignity, free enterprise, freedom of expression, elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because when there are elections, people tend to vote for peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They don’t vote for war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So we want to promote those principles around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We recognize that there are places of conflict in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We want to end those conflicts to the extent humanly possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But in order to be able to fulfill our role in the world, America must be strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: America must lead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And for that to happen, we have to strengthen our economy here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can’t have 23 million people struggling to get a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can’t have an economy that over the last three years keeps slowing down its growth rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can’t have kids coming out of college, half of them can’t find a job today, or a job that’s commensurate with their college degree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to get our economy going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And our military, we’ve got to strengthen our military long-term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know what the world is going to throw at us down the road.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We — we make decisions today in the military that — that will confront challenges we can’t imagine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In the 2000 debates, there was no mention of terrorism, for instance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And a year later, 9/11 happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So, we have to make decisions based upon uncertainty, and that means a strong military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will not cut our military budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to also stand by our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I think the tension that existed between Israel and the United States was very unfortunate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think also that pulling our missile defense program out of Poland in the way we did was also unfortunate in terms of, if you will, disrupting the relationship in some ways that existed between us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then, of course, with regards to standing for our principles, when — when the students took to the streets in Tehran and the people there protested, the Green Revolution occurred, for the president to be silent I thought was an enormous mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to stand for our principles, stand for our allies, stand for a strong military and stand for a stronger economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: America remains the one indispensable nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the world needs a strong America, and it is stronger now than when I came into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because we ended the war in Iraq, we were able to refocus our attention on not only the terrorist threat, but also beginning a transition process in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It also allowed us to refocus on alliances and relationships that had been neglected for a decade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Governor Romney, our alliances have never been stronger, in Asia, in Europe, in Africa, with Israel, where we have unprecedented military and intelligence cooperation, including dealing with the Iranian threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what we also have been able to do is position ourselves so we can start rebuilding America, and that’s what my plan does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Making sure that we’re bringing manufacturing back to our shores so that we’re creating jobs here, as we’ve done with the auto industry, not rewarding companies that are shipping jobs overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Making sure that we’ve got the best education system in the world, including retraining our workers for the jobs of tomorrow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Doing everything we can to control our own energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve cut our oil imports to the lowest level in two decades because we’ve developed oil and natural gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to develop clean energy technologies that will allow us to cut our exports in half by 2020.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of leadership that we need to show.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to make sure that we reduce our deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, Governor Romney’s plan doesn’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to do it in a responsible way by cutting out spending we don’t need, but also asking the wealthiest to pay a little bit more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That way we can invest in the research and technology that’s always kept us at the cutting edge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney has taken a different approach throughout this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Both at home and abroad, he has proposed wrong and reckless policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He’s praised George Bush as a good economic steward and Dick Cheney as somebody who’s — who shows great wisdom and judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And taking us back to those kinds of strategies that got us into this mess are not the way that we are going to maintain leadership in the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a policy for the future and agenda for the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to our economy here at home, I know what it takes to create 12 million new jobs and rising take-home pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what we’ve seen over the last four years is something I don’t want to see over the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president said by now we’d be a 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 4 percent unemployment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re 9 million jobs short of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will get America working again and see rising take-home pay again, and I’ll do it with five simple steps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number one, we are going to have North American energy independence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to do it by taking full advantage of oil, coal, gas, nuclear and our renewables.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we’re going to increase our trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Trade grows about 12 percent year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It doubles about every — every five or so years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We can do better than that, particularly in Latin America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The opportunities for us in Latin America we have just not taken advantage of fully.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, Latin America’s economy is almost as big as the economy of China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re all focused on China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Latin America is a huge opportunity for us — time zone, language opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number three, we’re going to have to have training programs that work for our workers and schools that finally put the parents and the teachers and the kids first, and the teachers’ unions going to have to go behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then we’re going to have to get to a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We can’t expect entrepreneurs and businesses large and small to take their life savings or their company’s money and invest in America if they think we’re headed to the road to Greece.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that’s where we’re going right now unless we finally get off this spending and borrowing binge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll get us on track to a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And finally, number five, we’ve got to champion small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Small business is where jobs come from.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Two-thirds of our jobs come from small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: New business formation is down to the lowest level in 30 years under this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to bring it back and get back good jobs and rising take-home pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, let’s talk about what we need to compete.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, Governor Romney talks about small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, Governor, when you were in Massachusetts, small businesses development ranked about 48th, I think out of 50 states in Massachusetts, because the policies that you are promoting actually don’t help small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the way you define small businesses includes folks at the very top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they include you and me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the kind of small business promotion we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But let’s take an example that we know is going to make a difference in the 21st century and that’s our education policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t have a lot of chance to talk about this in the last debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, under my leadership, what we’ve done is reformed education, working with governors, 46 states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve seen progress and gains in schools that were having a terrible time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they’re starting to finally make progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I now want to do is to hire more teachers, especially in math and science, because we know that we’ve fallen behind when it comes to math and science.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And those teachers can make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney, when you were asked by teachers whether or not this would help the economy grow, you said this isn’t going to help the economy grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When you were asked about reduced class sizes, you said class sizes don’t make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I tell you, if you talk to teachers, they will tell you it does make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we’ve got math teachers who are able to provide the kind of support that they need for our kids, that’s what’s going to determine whether or not the new businesses are created here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Companies are going to locate here depending on whether we’ve got the most highly skilled workforce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the kinds of budget proposals that you’ve put forward, when we don’t ask either you or me to pay a dime more in terms of reducing the deficit, but instead we slash support for education, that’s undermining our long-term competitiveness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is not good for America’s position in the world, and the world notices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well — well, I need to speak a moment…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … if you’ll let me, Bob, just about education…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … because I’m — I’m so proud of the state that I had the chance to be governor of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have every two years tests that look at how well our kids are doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Fourth graders and eighth graders are tested in English and math.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: While I was governor, I was proud that our fourth graders came out number one of all 50 states in English, and then also in math.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And our eighth graders number one in English and also in math.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First time one state had been number one in all four measures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How did we do that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, Republicans and Democrats came together on a bipartisan basis to put in place education principles that focused on having great teachers in the classroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ten years earlier…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that was — that was — that was what allowed us to become the number one state in the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But that was 10 years before you took office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then you cut education spending when you came into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The first — the first — the first — and we kept our schools number one in the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re still number one today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the principles that we put in place, we also gave kids not just a graduation exam that determined whether they were up to the skills needed to — to be able compete, but also if they graduated the quarter of their class, they got a four-year tuition- free ride at any Massachusetts public institution of higher learning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That happened before you came into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That was actually mine, actually, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You got that fact wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, let’s come back and talk about the military, but all the way — all the way through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I’m going through from the very beginning — we’re going to cut about 5 percent of the discretionary budget, excluding military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The good news is .

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d be happy to have you take a look.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Come on our website.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You look at how we get to a balanced budget within eight to 10 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We do it by getting — by reducing spending in a whole series of programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: By the way, number one I get rid of is Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are a number of things that sound good, but frankly, we just can’t afford them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that one doesn’t sound good and it’s not affordable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I’d get rid of that one from day one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: To the extent humanly possible, we get that out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We take program after program that we don’t absolutely have to have, and we get rid of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we take some programs that we are doing to keep, like Medicaid, which is a program for the poor; we’ll take that healthcare program for the poor and we give it to the states to run because states run these programs more efficiently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a governor, I thought please, give me this program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can run this more efficiently than the federal government and states, by the way, are proving it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: States like Arizona, Rhode Island have taken these — these Medicaid dollars; have shown they can run these programs more cost-effectively.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to do those two things and get this — get this to a balanced budget with eight — eight to 10 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the military — let’s get back to the military, though.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: SCHIEFFER: That’s what I’m trying…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He should have answered the first question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, Governor Romney’s called for $5 trillion of tax cuts that he says he’s going to pay for by closing deductions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, the math doesn’t work, but he continues to claim that he’s going to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He then wants to spend another $2 trillion on military spending that our military is not asking for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, keep in mind that our military spending has gone up every single year that I’ve been in office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We spend more on our military than the next 10 countries combined; China, Russia, France, the United Kingdom, you name it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The next 10.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I did was work with our joint chiefs of staff to think about, what are we going to need in the future to make sure that we are safe?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the budget that we’ve put forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, what you can’t do is spend $2 trillion in additional military spending that the military is not asking for, $5 trillion on tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You say that you’re going to pay for it by closing loopholes and deductions, without naming what those loopholes and deductions are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And then somehow you’re also going to deal with the deficit that we’ve already got.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The math simply doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when it comes to our military, what we have to think about is not, you know just budgets, we’ve got to think about capabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need to be thinking about cyber security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need to be talking about space.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly what our budget does, but it’s driven by strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not driven by politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not driven by members of Congress, and what they would like to see.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s driven by, what are we going to need to keep the American people safe?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly what our budget does, and it also then allows us to reduce our deficit, which is a significant national security concern.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because we’ve got to make sure that our economy is strong at home so that we can project military power overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m pleased that I’ve balanced budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was on the world of business for 25 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If you didn’t balance your budget, you went out of business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I went into the Olympics that was out of balance, and we got it on balance, and made a success there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I had the chance to be governor of a state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Four years in a row, Democrats and Republicans came together to balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We cut taxes 19 times and balanced our budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president hasn’t balanced a budget yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I expect to have the opportunity to do so myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to be able to balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about military spending, and that’s this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our Navy is old — excuse me, our Navy is smaller now than at any time since 1917.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The Navy said they needed 313 ships to carry out their mission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re now at under 285.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re headed down to the low 200s if we go through a sequestration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s unacceptable to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure that we have the ships that are required by our Navy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our Air Force is older and smaller than at any time since it was founded in 1947.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve changed for the first time since FDR — since FDR we had the — we’ve always had the strategy of saying we could fight in two conflicts at once.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now we’re changing to one conflict.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, this, in my view, is the highest responsibility of the President of the United States, which is to maintain the safety of the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I will not cut our military budget by a trillion dollars, which is a combination of the budget cuts the president has, as well as the sequestration cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That, in my view, is making — is making our future less certain and less secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bob, I just need to comment on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, the sequester is not something that I’ve proposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is something that Congress has proposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It will not happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The budget that we are talking about is not reducing our military spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is maintaining it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think Governor Romney maybe hasn’t spent enough time looking at how our military works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You mentioned the Navy, for example, and that we have fewer ships than we did in 1916.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Governor, we also have fewer horses and bayonets, because the nature of our military’s changed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have these things called aircraft carriers, where planes land on them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have these ships that go underwater, nuclear submarines.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so the question is not a game of Battleship, where we’re counting slips.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s what are our capabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so when I sit down with the Secretary of the Navy and the Joint Chiefs of Staff, we determine how are we going to be best able to meet all of our defense needs in a way that also keeps faith with our troops, that also makes sure that our veterans have the kind of support that they need when they come home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that is not reflected in the kind of budget that you’re putting forward because it just doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, we visited the website quite a bit and it still doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, Israel is a true friend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is our greatest ally in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if Israel is attacked, America will stand with Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve made that clear throughout my presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I will stand with Israel if they are attacked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is the reason why, working with Israel, we have created the strongest military and intelligence cooperation between our two countries in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, this week we’ll be carrying out the largest military exercise with Israel in history, this very week.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But to the issue of Iran, as long as I’m president of the United States Iran will not get a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I made that clear when I came into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We then organized the strongest coalition and the strongest sanctions against Iran in history, and it is crippling their economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Their currency has dropped 80 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Their oil production has plunged to the lowest level since they were fighting a war with Iraq 20 years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So their economy is in a shambles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason we did this is because a nuclear Iran is a threat to our national security, and it is a threat to Israel’s national security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We cannot afford to have a nuclear arms race in the most volatile region of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Iran is a state sponsor of terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And for them to be able to provide nuclear technology to non-state actors, that’s unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they have said that they want to see Israel wiped off the map.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So the work that we’ve done with respect to sanctions now offers Iran a choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They can take the diplomatic route and end their nuclear program or they will have to face a united world and a United States president, me, who said we’re not going to take any options off the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The disagreement I have with Governor Romney is that, during the course of this campaign, he’s often talked as if we should take premature military action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that would be a mistake, because when I’ve sent young men and women into harm’s way, I always understand that that is the last resort, not the first resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I want to underscore the same point the president mad,e which is that if I’m President of the United States, when I’m President of the United States, we will stand with Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if Israel is attacked, we have their back, not just diplomatically, not just culturally, but militarily.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, with regards to Iran and the threat of Iran, there’s no question but that a nuclear Iran, a nuclear-capable Iran is unacceptable to America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It presents a threat not only to our friends but ultimately a threat to us to have Iran have nuclear material, nuclear weapons that could be used against us or used to be threatening to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It is also essential for us to understand what our mission is in Iran, and that is to dissuade Iran from having a nuclear weapon through peaceful and diplomatic means.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And crippling sanctions are something I called for five years ago, when I was in Israel, speaking at the Herzliya Conference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I laid out seven steps, crippling sanctions were number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And they do work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’re seeing it right now in the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s absolutely the right thing to do, to have crippling sanctions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I would have put them in place earlier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But it’s good that we have them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, something I would add today is I would tighten those sanctions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I would say that ships that carry Iranian oil, can’t come into our ports.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I imagine the E.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: would agree with us as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Not only ships couldn’t, but I’d say companies that are moving their oil can’t, people who are trading in their oil can’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I would tighten those sanctions further.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, I’d take on diplomatic isolation efforts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d make sure that Ahmadinejad is indicted under the Genocide Convention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: His words amount to genocide incitation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I would indict him for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I would also make sure that their diplomats are treated like the pariah they are around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The same way we treated the apartheid diplomats of South Africa.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to increase pressure time, and time again on Iran because anything other than a — a — a solution to this, which says — which stops this — this nuclear folly of theirs, is unacceptable to America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And of course, a military action is the last resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It is something one would only – only consider if all of the other avenues had been — had been tried to their full extent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all those are reports in the newspaper.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But our goal is to get Iran to recognize it needs to give up its nuclear program and abide by the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: resolutions that have been in place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because they have the opportunity to reenter the community of nations, and we would welcome that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There — there are people in Iran who have the same aspirations as people all around the world for a better life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we hope that their leadership takes the right decision, but the deal we’ll accept is they end their nuclear program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s very straightforward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’m glad that Governor Romney agrees with the steps that we’re taking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, there have been times, Governor, frankly, during the course of this campaign, where it sounded like you thought that you’d do the same things we did, but you’d say them louder and somehow that — that would make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it turns out that the work involved in setting up these crippling sanctions is painstaking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s meticulous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We started from the day we got into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason is was so important — and this is a testament to how we’ve restored American credibility and strength around the world — is we had to make sure that all the countries participated, even countries like Russia and China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because if it’s just us that are imposing sanctions — we’ve had sanctions in place a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s because we got everybody to agree that Iran is seeing so much pressure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to maintain that pressure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There is a deal to be had, and that is that they abide by the rules that have already been established.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They convince the international community they are not pursuing a nuclear program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There are inspections that are very intrusive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But over time, what they can do is regain credibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the meantime, though, we’re not going to let up the pressure until we have clear evidence that that takes place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one last thing — just — just to make this point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The clock is ticking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to allow Iran to perpetually engage in negotiations that lead nowhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been very clear to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, because of the intelligence coordination that we do with a range of countries, including Israel, we have a sense of when they would get breakout capacity, which means that we would not be able to intervene in time to stop their nuclear program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that clock is ticking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
