transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to make sure that if they do not meet the demands of the international community, then we are going to take all options necessary to make sure they don’t have a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think from the very beginning, one of the challenges we’ve had with Iran is that they have looked at this administration, and felt that the administration was not as strong as it needed to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think they saw weakness where they had expected to find American strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I say that because from the very beginning, the president in his campaign four years ago, said he would meet with all the world’s worst actors in his first year, he’d sit down with Chavez and Kim Jong-il, with Castro and President Ahmadinejad of Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I think they looked and thought, well, that’s an unusual honor to receive from the President of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then the president began what I have called an apology tour, of going to various nations in the Middle East and criticizing America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think they looked at that and saw weakness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Then when there were dissidents in the streets of Tehran, a Green Revolution, holding signs saying, is America with us, the president was silent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think they noticed that as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I think that when the president said he was going to create daylight between ourselves and Israel, that they noticed that as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: All of these things suggested, I think, to the Iranian mullahs that, hey, you know, we can keep on pushing along here, we can keep talks going on, we’re just going to keep on spinning centrifuges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now there are some 10,000 centrifuges spinning uranium, preparing to create a nuclear threat to the United States and to the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s unacceptable for us, and it’s essential for a president to show strength from the very beginning, to make it very clear what is acceptable and not acceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And an Iranian nuclear program is not acceptable to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They must not develop nuclear capability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the way to make sure they understand that is by having, from the very beginning, the tightest sanctions possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They need to be tightened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our diplomatic isolation needs to be tougher.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to indict Ahmadinejad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to put the pressure on them as hard as we possibly can, because if we do that, we won’t have to take the military action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bob, let me just respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nothing Governor Romney just said is true, starting with this notion of me apologizing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This has been probably the biggest whopper that’s been told during the course of this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And every fact checker and every reporter who’s looked at it, Governor, has said this is not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to tightening sanctions, look, as I said before, we’ve put in the toughest, most crippling sanctions ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the fact is, while we were coordinating an international coalition to make sure these sanctions were effective, you were still invested in a Chinese state oil company that was doing business with the Iranian oil sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So I’ll let the American people decide, judge, who’s going to be more effective and more credible when it comes to imposing crippling sanctions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And with respect to our attitude about the Iranian revolution, I was very clear about the murderous activities that had taken place and that was contrary to international law and everything that civilized people stand for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And — and so the strength that we have shown in Iran is shown by the fact that we’ve been able to mobilize the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When I came into office, the world was divided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Iran was resurgent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Iran is at its weakest point, economically, strategically, militarily, then since — then in many years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are going to continue to keep the pressure on to make sure that they do not get a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s in America’s national interest and that will be the case so long as I’m president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re four years closer to a nuclear Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re four years closer to a nuclear Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and — we should not have wasted these four years to the extent they — they continue to be able to spin these centrifuges and get that much closer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, the reason I call it an apology tour is because you went to the Middle East and you flew to Egypt and to Saudi Arabia and to Turkey and Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, you skipped Israel, our closest friend in the region, but you went to the other nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, they noticed that you skipped Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then in those nations, and on Arabic TV, you said that America had been dismissive and derisive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You said that on occasion America had dictated to other nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, America has not dictated to other nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have freed other nations from dictators.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bob, let me — let me respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we’re going to talk about trips that we’ve taken — when I was a candidate for office, first trip I took was to visit our troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when I went to Israel as a candidate, I didn’t take donors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t attend fundraisers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I went to Yad Beshef , the Holocaust museum there, to remind myself the nature of evil and why our bond with Israel will be unbreakable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And then I went down to the border towns of Storok , which had experienced missiles raining dowm from Hamas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I saw families there who showed me there where missiles had come down near their children’s bedrooms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I was reminded of what that would mean if those were my kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Which is why as president, we funded an Iron Dome program to stop those missiles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So that’s how I’ve used my travels, when I travel to Israel and when I travel to the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the — the central question at this point is going to be: Who is going to be credible to all parties involved?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they can look at my track record, whether it’s Iran sanctions, whether it’s dealing with counterterrorism, whether it’s supporting democracy, whether it’s supporting women’s rights, whether it’s supporting religious minorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they can say that the President of the United States and the United States of America has stood on the right side of history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that kind of credibility is precisely why we’ve been able to show leadership on a wide range of issues facing the world right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Bob, let’s not go into hypotheticals of that nature.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our relationship with Israel, my relationship with the prime minister of Israel is such that we would not get a call saying our bombers are on the way, or their fighters are on the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is the kind of thing that would have been discussed and thoroughly evaluated well before that kind of —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let me — let me come back — we can come back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s come back to what the president was speaking about, which is what’s happening in the world and the president’s statement that things are going so well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, I look at what’s happening around the world, and i see Iran four years closer to a bomb.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I see the Middle East with a rising tide of violence, chaos, tumult.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I see jihadists continuing to spread, whether they’re rising or just about the same level, hard to precisely measure, but it’s clear they’re there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re very strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I see Syria with 30,000 civilians dead, Assad still in power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I see our trade deficit with China, larger than it’s — growing larger every year, as a matter of fact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I look around the world and I don’t feel that you see North Korea, continuing to export their nuclear technology, Russia said they’re not going to follow Nunn-Lugar any more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re back away from a nuclear proliferation treaty that we had with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I look around the world, I don’t see our influence growing around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I see our influence receding, in part because of the failure of the president to deal with our economic challenges at home; in part because of our withdrawal from our commitment to our military in the way I think it ought to be; in part because of the — the — the turmoil with Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I mean, the president received a letter from 38 Democrat senators saying the tensions with Israel were a real problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They asked him, please repair the tension — Democrat senators — please repair the tension…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … the damage in his — in his own party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor, the problem is, is that on a whole range of issues, whether it’s the Middle East, whether it’s Afghanistan, whether it’s Iraq, whether it’s now Iran, you’ve been all over the map.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, I’m — I’m pleased that you now are endorsing our policy of applying diplomatic pressure and potentially having bilateral discussions with the Iranians to end their nuclear program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But just a few years ago you said that’s something you’d never do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the same way that you initially opposed a timetable in Afghanistan, now you’re for it, although it depends.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the same way that you say you would have ended the war in Iraq, but recently gave a speech saying that we should have 20,000 more folks in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The same way that you said that it was mission creep to go after Gadhafi.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to going after Osama bin Laden, you said, well, any president would make that call.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when you were a candidate in 2008, as I was, and I said if I got bin Laden in our sights I would take that shot, you said we shouldn’t move heaven and earth to get one man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you said we should ask Pakistan for permission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we had asked Pakistan permission, we would not have gotten him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it was worth moving heaven and earth to get him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, after we killed bin Laden I was at ground zero for a memorial and talked to a young women who was four years old when 9/11 happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the last conversation she had with her father was him calling from the twin towers, saying “Peyton , I love you and I will always watch over you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And for the next decade, she was haunted by that conversation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And she said to me, “You know, by finally getting bin Laden, that brought some closure to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And when we do things like that — when we bring those who have harmed us to justice, that sends a message to the world and it tells Peyton that we did not forget her father.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I make that point because that’s the kind of clarity of leadership, and those decisions are not always popular.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Those decisions generally — generally are not poll-tested.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And even some in my own party, including my current vice president, had the same critique as you did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what the American people understand is that I look at what we need to get done to keep the American people safe and to move our interests forward, and I make those decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Bob…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can’t — but you can’t have the president just lay out a whole series of items without giving me a chance to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s probably true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, we’re going to be finished by 2014, and when I’m president, we’ll make sure we bring our troops out by the end of 2014.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The commanders and the generals there are on track to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve seen progress over the past several years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The surge has been successful and the training program is proceeding apace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are now a large number of Afghan Security Forces, 350,000 that are ready to step in to provide security and we’re going to be able to make that transition by the end of 2014.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So our troops will come home at that point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can tell you at the same time, that we will make sure that we look at what’s happening in Pakistan, and recognize that what’s happening in Pakistan is going to have a major impact on the success in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I say that because I know a lot of people that feel like we should just brush our hands and walk away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t mean you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, but some people in the — in our nation feel that Pakistan is being nice to us, and that we should walk away fro mthem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But Pakistan is important to the region, to the world and to us, because Pakistan has 100 nuclear warheads and they’re rushing to build a lot more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’ll have more than Great Britain sometime in the — in the relatively near future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They also have the Haqqani Network and the Taliban existent within their country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so a Pakistan that falls apart, becomes a failed state, would be of extraordinary danger to Afghanistan and to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so we’re going to have to remain helpful in encouraging Pakistan to move towards a more stable government and rebuild the relationship with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that means that our aid that we provide to Pakistan is going to have to be conditioned upon certain benchmarks being met.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So for me, I look at this as both a need to help move Pakistan in the right direction, and also to get Afghanistan to be ready, and they will be ready by the end of 2014.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When I came into office, we were still bogged down in Iraq and Afghanistan had been drifting for a decade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We ended the war in Iraq, refocused our attention on Afghanistan, and we did deliver a surge of troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That was facilitated in part because we had ended the war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are now in a position where we have met many of the objectives that got us there in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Part of what had happened is we’d forgotten why we had gone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We went because there were people who were responsible for 3,000 American deaths.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so we decimated Al Qaida’s core leadership in the border regions between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We then started to build up Afghan forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’re now in a position where we can transition out, because there’s no reason why Americans should die when Afghans are perfectly capable of defending their own country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, that transition has to take place in a responsible fashion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been there a long time, and we’ve got to make sure that we and our coalition partners are pulling out responsibly and giving Afghans the capabilities that they need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what I think the American people recognize is after a decade of war it’s time to do some nation building here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what we can now do is free up some resources, to, for example, put Americans back to work, especially our veterans, rebuilding our roads, our bridges, our schools, making sure that, you know, our veterans are getting the care that they need when it comes to post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injury, making sure that the certifications that they need for good jobs of the future are in place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, I was having lunch with some — a veteran in Minnesota who had been a medic dealing with the most extreme circumstances.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When he came home and he wanted to become a nurse, he had to start from scratch.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what we’ve said is let’s change those certifications.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The first lady has done great work with an organization called Joining Forces putting our veterans back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence, veterans’ unemployment is actually now lower than general population.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It was higher when I came into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So those are the kinds of things that we can now do because we’re making that transition in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, it’s not time to divorce a nation on Earth that has 100 nuclear weapons and is on the way to double that at some point, a nation that has serious threats from terrorist groups within its nation, as I indicated before, the Taliban, Haqqani Network.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s a nation that’s not like — like others and it does not have a civilian leadership that is calling the shots there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You have the ISI, their intelligence organization, is probably the most powerful of the — of three branches there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Then you have the military and then you have the civilian government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a nation, which, if it falls apart, if it — if it becomes a failed state, there are nuclear weapons there and you’ve got — you’ve got terrorists there who could grab their — their hands onto those nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is — this is an important part of the world for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Pakistan is — is technically an ally, and they’re not acting very much like an ally right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But we have some work to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I — I don’t blame the administration for the fact that the relationship with Pakistan is strained.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We — we had to go into Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We had to go in there to get Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That was the right thing to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and that upset them, but obviously there was a great deal of anger even before that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But we’re going to have to work with the — with the people in Pakistan to try and help them move to a more responsible course than the one that they’re on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it’s important for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s important for the nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s important for the success of Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because inside Pakistan, you have a — a large group of Pashtun that are — that are Taliban.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to come rushing back in to Afghanistan when we go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that’s one of the reasons the Afghan Security Forces have so much work to do to be able to fight against that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But it’s important for us to recognize that we can’t just walk away from Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But we do need to make sure that as we — as we send support for them, that this is tied to them making progress on — on matters that would lead them to becoming a civil society.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well I believe we should use any and all means necessary to take out people who pose a threat to us and our friends around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it’s widely reported that drones are being used in drone strikes, and I support that and entirely, and feel the president was right to up the usage of that technology, and believe that we should continue to use it, to continue to go after the people that represent a threat to this nation and to our friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let me also note that as I said earlier, we’re going to have to do more than just going after leaders and — and killing bad guys, important as that is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re also going to have to have a farm more effective and comprehensive strategy to help move the world away from terror and Islamic extremism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t done that yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We talk a lot about these things, but you look at the — the record, you look at the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You look at the record of the last four years and say is Iran closer to a bomb?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Is the Middle East in tumult?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Is — is al-Qaida on the run, on its heels?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Is — are Israel and the Palestinians closer to reaching a peace agreement?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, they haven’t had talks in two years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have not seen the progress we need to have, and I’m convinced that with strong leadership and an effort to build a strategy based upon helping these nations reject extremism, we can see the kind of peace and prosperity the world demands.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, keep in mind our strategy wasn’t just going after bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We created partnerships throughout the region to deal with extremism in Somalia, in Yemen, in Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what we’ve also done is engaged these governments in the kind of reforms that are actually going to make a difference in people’s lives day to day, to make sure that their governments aren’t corrupt, to make sure that they’re treating women with the kind of respect and dignity that every nation that succeeds has shown and to make sure that they’ve got a free market system that works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So across the board, we are engaging them in building capacity in these countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we have stood on the side of democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: One thing I think Americans should be proud of, when Tunisians began to protest, this nation — me, my administration — stood with them earlier than just about any country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In Egypt we stood on the side of democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In Libya we stood on the side of the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence, there’s no doubt that attitudes about Americans have changed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there are always going to be elements in these countries that potentially threaten the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we want to shrink those groups and those networks and we can do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’re always also going to have to maintain vigilance when it comes to terrorist activities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The truth, though, is that Al Qaeda is much weaker than it was when I came into office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they don’t have the same capacities to attack the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: homeland and our allies as they did four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think it will continue to be terrorist networks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have to remain vigilant, as I just said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But with respect to China, China is both an adversary, but also a potential partner in the international community if it’s following the rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So my attitude coming into office was that we are going to insist that China plays by the same rules as everybody else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I know Americans had seen jobs being shipped overseas; businesses and workers not getting a level playing field when it came to trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the reason why I set up a trade task force to go after cheaters when it came to international trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the reason why we have brought more cases against China for violating trade rules than the other — the previous administration had done in two terms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve won just about every case that we’ve filed, that has been decided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, just recently steelworkers in Ohio and throughout the Midwest — Pennsylvania — are in a position now to sell steel to China because we won that case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We had a tire case in which they were flooding us with cheap domestic tires — or — or cheap Chinese tires.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we put a stop to it and as a consequence saved jobs throughout America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I have to say that Governor Romney criticized me for being too tough in that tire case; said this wouldn’t be good for American workers and that it would be protectionist.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I tell you, those workers don’t feel that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They feel as if they had finally an administration who was going to take this issue seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Over the long term, in order for us to compete with China, we’ve also got to make sure, though, that we’re taking — taking care of business here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we don’t have the best education system in the world, if we don’t continue to put money into research and technology that will allow us to create great businesses here in the United States, that’s how we lose the competition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, unfortunately, Governor Romney’s budget and his proposals would not allow us to make those investments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, it’s not government that makes business successful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not government investments that makes businesses grow and hire people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me also note that the greatest threat that the world faces, the greatest national security threat is a nuclear Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: China has an interest that’s very much like ours in one respect, and that is they want a stable world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want to see protectionism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want to see the world break out into — into various forms of chaos, because they have to — they have to manufacture goods and put people to work and they have about 20,000 — 20 million, rather, people coming out of the farms every year coming into the cities, needing jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So they want the economy to work and the world to be free and open.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so we can be a partner with China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to be an adversary in any way, shape or form.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We can work with them, we can collaborate with them, if they’re willing to be responsible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, they look at us and say, Is it a good idea to be with America?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How strong are we going to be?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How strong is our economy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They look at the fact that we owe ’em a trillion dollars and owe other people $16 trillion in total, including that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They look at our — our decision to — to cut back on our military capabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A trillion dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not my term, it’s the president’s own secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not my term, it’s the president’s own Secretary of Defense, called them devastating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They look at America’s commitments around the world and they see what’s happening, and they say, well, OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Is America going to be strong?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the answer is, yes, if I’m president, America will be very strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ll also make sure that we have trade relations with China that work for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve watched year in and year out as companies have shut down and people have lost their jobs because China has not played by the same rules, in part by holding down artificially the value of their currency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It holds down the prices of their goods.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It means our goods aren’t as competitive and we lose jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s got to end.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re making some progress; they need to make more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s why on day one, i will label them a currency manipulator, which allows us to apply tariffs where they’re taking jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re stealing our intellectual property, our patents, our designs, our technology, hacking into our computers, counterfeiting our goods.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They have to understand we want to trade with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We want a world that’s stable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We like free enterprise, but you got to play by the rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, they sell us about this much stuff every year, and we sell them about this much stuff every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So it’s pretty clear who doesn’t want a trade war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there’s one going on right now, which we don’t know about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s a silent one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And they’re winning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have enormous trade imbalance with China, and it’s worse this year than last year, and it’s worse last year than the year before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so we have to understand that we can’t just surrender and lose jobs year in and year out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to say to our friend in China, look, you guys are playing aggressively.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We understand it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But this can’t keep on going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can’t keep on holding down the value of your currency, stealing our intellectual property, counterfeiting our products, selling them around the world, even to the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was with one company that makes valves and — and process industries and they said, look, we were — we were having some valves coming in that — that were broken and we had to repair them under warranty and we looked them and — and they had our serial number on them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then we noticed that there was more than one with that same serial number.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They were counterfeit products being made overseas with the same serial number as a U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: company, the same packaging, these were being sold into our market and around the world as if they were made by the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: competitor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This can’t go on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want a great relationship with China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: China can be our partner, but — but that doesn’t mean they can just roll all over us and steal our jobs on an unfair basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Governor Romney’s right, you are familiar with jobs being shipped overseas because you invested in companies that were shipping jobs overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, that’s — you’re right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean that’s how our free market works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I’ve made a different bet on American workers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we had taken your advice Governor Romney about our auto industry, we’d be buying cars from China instead of selling cars to China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we take your advice with respect to how we change our tax codes so that companies that earn profits overseas don’t pay U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: taxes compared to companies here that are paying taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now that’s estimated to create 800,000 jobs, the problem is they won’t be here, they’ll be in places like China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we’re not making investments in education and basic research, which is not something that the private sector is doing at a sufficient pace right now and has never done, then we will lose the in things like clean energy technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now with respect to what we’ve done with China already, U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: exports have doubled since I came into office, to China and actually currencies are at their most advantageous point for U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: exporters since 1993.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We absolutely have to make more progress and that’s why we’re going to keep on pressing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to our military and Chinese security, part of the reason that we were able to pivot to the Asia-Pacific region after having ended the war in Iraq and transitioning out of Afghanistan, is precisely because this is going to be a massive growth area in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we believe China can be a partner, but we’re also sending a very clear signal that America is a Pacific power; that we are going to have a presence there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are working with countries in the region to make sure, for example, that ships can pass through; that commerce continues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’re organizing trade relations with countries other than China so that China starts feeling more pressure about meeting basic international standards.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of leadership we’ve shown in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of leadership that we’ll continue to show.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I just want to take one of those points, again, attacking me as not talking about an agenda for — for getting more trade and opening up more jobs in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the president mentioned the auto industry and that somehow I would be in favor of jobs being elsewhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Nothing could be further from the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m a son of Detroit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was born in Detroit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My dad was head of a car company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I like American cars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I would do nothing to hurt the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: auto industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My plan to get the industry on its feet when it was in real trouble was not to start writing checks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It was President Bush that wrote the first checks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I disagree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I said they need — these companies need to go through a managed bankruptcy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And in that process, they can get government help and government guarantees, but they need to go through bankruptcy to get rid of excess cost and the debt burden that they’d — they’d built up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And fortunately…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney, that’s not what you said…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney, you did not…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can take a look at the op-ed…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You did not say that you would provide government help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I said that we would provide guarantees, and — and that was what was able to allow these companies to go through bankruptcy, to come out of bankruptcy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Under no circumstances would I do anything other than to help this industry get on its feet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the idea that has been suggested that I would liquidate the industry, of course not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Of course not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s check the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s the height of silliness…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let — let — let’s…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I have never said I would liquidate…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …I would liquidate the industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor, the people in Detroit don’t forget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …and — and that’s why I have the kind of commitment to ensure that our industries in this country can compete and be successful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We in this country can — can compete successfully with anyone in the world, and we’re going to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to have a president, however, that doesn’t think that somehow the government investing in — in car companies like Tesla and — and Fisker, making electric battery cars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is not research, Mr President, these are the government investing in companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Investing in Solyndra.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a company, this isn’t basic research.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I want to invest in research.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Research is great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Providing funding to universities and think tanks is great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But investing in companies?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s the wrong way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The fact of the matter is…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m still speaking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I want to make sure that we make — we make America more competitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Yeah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that we do those things that make America the most attractive place in the world for entrepreneurs, innovators, businesses to grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But you’re investing in companies doesn’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In fact it makes it less likely for them to come here…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …because the private sector’s not going to invest in a…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m — I’m — I’m happy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …company…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …to respond to you…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …if — if you’re…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …you’ve had the floor for a while.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …get someone else’s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: OBAMA: The — look, I think anybody out there can check the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney, you keep on trying to, you know airbrush history here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You were very clear that you would not provide, government assistance to the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: auto companies, even if they went through bankruptcy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You said that they could get it in the private marketplace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They would have gone through a…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’re wrong…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …they would have gone through a…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …you’re wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, I am not wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I am not wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: People can look it up, you’re right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: People will look it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But more importantly it is true that in order for us to be competitive, we’re going to have to make some smart choices right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Cutting our education budget, that’s not a smart choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That will not help us compete with China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Cutting our investments in research and technology, that’s not a smart choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That will not help us compete with China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bringing down our deficit by adding $7 trillion of tax cuts and military spending that our military is not asking for, before we even get to the debt that we currently have, that is not going to make us more competitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Those are the kinds of choices that the American people face right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Having a tax code that rewards companies that are shipping jobs overseas instead of companies that are investing here in the United States, that will not make us more competitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the one thing that I’m absolutely clear about is that after a decade in which we saw drift, jobs being shipped overseas, nobody championing American workers and American businesses, we’ve now begun to make some real progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we can’t do is go back to the same policies that got us into such difficulty in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we have to move forward and not go back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I couldn’t agree more about going forward, but I certainly don’t want to go back to the policies of the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The policies of the last four years have seen incomes in America decline every year for middle income families, now down $4,300 during your term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Twenty-three million Americans still struggling to find a good job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When you came to office 32 million people on food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Today, 47 million people on food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When you came to office, just over $10 trillion in debt, now $16 trillion in debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It hasn’t worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You said by now we’d be at 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 4 percent unemployment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re 9 million jobs short of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met some of those people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met them in Appleton, Wisconsin.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I met a young woman in — in Philadelphia who’s coming out of — out of college, can’t find work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been — Ann was with someone just the other day that was just weeping about not being able to get work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s just a tragedy in a nation so prosperous as ours, that the last four years have been so hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why it’s so critical, that we make America once again the most attractive place in the world to start businesses, to build jobs, to grow the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that’s not going to happen by just hiring teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, I love to — I love teachers, and I’m happy to have states and communities that want to hire teachers do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: By the way, I don’t like to have the federal government start pushing its weight deeper and deeper into our schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let the states and localities do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was a governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The federal government didn’t hire our teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I love teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I want to get our private sector growing and I know how to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you very much, Bob, Governor Romney, and to Lynn University.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ve now heard three debates, months of campaigning and way too many TV commercials.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And now you’ve got a choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Over the last four years we’ve made real progress digging our way out of policies that gave us two prolonged wars, record deficits and the worst economic crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Governor Romney wants to take us back to those policies, a foreign policy that’s wrong and reckless, economic policies that won’t create jobs, won’t reduce our deficit, but will make sure that folks at the very top don’t have to play by the same rules that you do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve got a different vision for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to build on our strengths.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve put forward a plan to make sure that we’re bringing manufacturing jobs back to our shores by rewarding companies and small businesses that are investing here, not overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure we’ve got the best education system in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’re retaining our workers for the jobs of tomorrow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to control our own energy by developing oil and natural gas but also the energy sources of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I want to reduce our deficit by cutting spending that we don’t need but also by asking the wealthy to do a little bit more so that we can invest in things like research and technology that are the key to a 21st century economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: As Commander in Chief, I will maintain the strongest military in the world, keep faith with our troops and go after those who would do us harm.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: but after a decade of war, I think we all recognize we’ve got to do some nation building here at home, rebuilding our roads, our bridges and especially caring for our Veterans who sacrificed so much for our freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve been through tough times but we always bounce back because of our character, because we pull together and if I have the privilege of being your president for another four years, I promise you I will always listen to your voices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I will fight for your families and I will work every single day to make sure that America continues to be the greatest nation on earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Bob, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, folks at Lynn University, good to be with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m optimistic about the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m excited about our prospects as a nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to see peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to see growing peace in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s our objective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have an opportunity to have real leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: America’s going to have that kind of leadership and continue to promote principles of peace to make a world a safer place and make people in this country more confident that their future is secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I also want to make sure that we get this economy going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there are two very different paths the country can take.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One is a path represented by the president, which at the end of four years would mean we’d have $20 trillion in debt heading towards Greece.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get us on track to a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s path will mean continuing declining in take-home pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure our take-home pay turns around and starts to grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s path will mean continuing declining in take-home pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure take-home pay turns around and starts to grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s path means 20 million people out of work struggling for a good job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get people back to work with 12 million new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to make sure that we get people off of food stamps, not by cutting the program, but by getting them good jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: America’s going to come back, and for that to happen, we’re going to have to have a president who can work across the aisle.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was in a state where my legislature was 87 percent Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I learned how to get along on the other side of the aisle.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to do that in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Washington is broken.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to get this country back, and will work with good Democrats and good Republicans to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This nation is the hope of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been blessed by having a nation that’s free and prosperous thanks to the contributions of the greatest generation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’ve held a torch for the world to see — the torch of freedom and hope and opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, it’s our turn to take that torch.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m convinced we’ll do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need strong leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to be that leader with your support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll work with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll lead you in an open and honest way, and I ask for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to be the next president of the United States to support and help this great nation and to make sure that we all together remain America as the hope of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you so much.
